runs.goal_hypothesis: Establish whether potential shaping at coefficient 0.01 supports robust heuristic play in the 8.192M-step regimen.

results_insights.insight: High generic-heuristic success masked severe defensive/offensive weakness.

reasoning: Shaping supported generic play but not broad robustness.
This first group run defines several configuration knobs, so it is not a clean coefficient-only comparison.
100-game side evaluations carry sampling noise, especially for low rates.

runs.goal_hypothesis: Remove potential shaping while holding the 8.192M-step regimen fixed, relative to 48afd570381e4f05aa0526d9c9c2e396.

results_insights.insight: No shaping improved aggregate win rate by 0.1967 over the shaped control.
Worst-side win rate rose from 0.03 to 0.07.
Strong offensive-X play contrasted with only 7% offensive-O.

reasoning: Removing 0.01 shaping improved this controlled terminal comparison.
Large side asymmetry shows aggregate improvement was not uniformly robust.
Independent stochastic training and finite evaluation remain alternative explanations without replications.

runs.goal_hypothesis: Replicate the unshaped configuration of a952747d491342d4a391cf3951773aae with richer evaluation metrics.

results_insights.insight: Replication was 0.0433 below the preceding unshaped run but remained above the original shaped control.
Worst-side robustness varied sharply across replications.
The richer logger shows defensive-O games lasted 15.3 moves on average despite only 2% wins.

reasoning: The unshaped aggregate advantage broadly replicated, but worst-case performance did not.
Seed/training stochasticity likely explains part of the difference between nominally identical runs.
Episode-length evidence was newly logged and cannot be compared to older runs lacking that metric.

runs.goal_hypothesis: Retest coefficient-0.01 shaping with richer metrics in a shortened 5.12M-step schedule, relative to the richer unshaped run dde04e6209cd40f9ad02cd7341e56675.

results_insights.insight: Aggregate was 0.02 above the richer unshaped run despite substantially shorter training.
At least one side had no wins, so robustness did not improve.
Defensive-X games were prolonged but still had 0% wins.

reasoning: Shaping may accelerate aggregate learning but did not resolve worst-case failure.
Duration and curriculum boundaries changed alongside shaping, so this is not controlled.
Longer episodes can indicate resistance without competence and should not be interpreted as wins.

runs.goal_hypothesis: Test weaker coefficient-0.001 shaping under the same shortened schedule as f7caf4ff76bf4109940c86e7aaff0bea.

results_insights.insight: Worst-side rate modestly exceeded the zero of coefficient 0.01.
Defensive-X games lasted longer but ended in only 1% wins.

reasoning: Coefficient 0.001 traded a tiny aggregate decline for a tiny worst-rate increase.
The controlled coefficient comparison supports no decisive advantage at this sample size.
Training stochasticity and 100-game evaluation noise can readily explain percentage-point differences.

runs.goal_hypothesis: Test whether doubling defensive potential weight improves robustness over the shortened shaping variants.

results_insights.insight: Defense-biased shaping underperformed both coefficient-0.01 and coefficient-0.001 shortened runs.
Long defensive games still ended with 0% wins as O.

reasoning: Defense weighting prolonged defensive games but did not yield defensive wins.
Both coefficient and defense weight differ from the weak-shaping predecessor, confounding their effects.
Episode duration is not a substitute for win-rate competence; stochastic variation remains possible.
